text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A Riga court started to hear the case of Rustem Kadirov and his associates from the Tess Petroleum group, accused of smuggling fuel into Latvia.
- About 100 people including several MPs held a rally in the centre of Riga in memory of Dzhokhar Dudayev, the late Chechen leader.
- Vereinsbank Riga, a subsidiary of Vereins-Westbank AG, has officially started its operations in Latvia.

- Prime ministers of the three Baltic republics will meet in Parnu on April 26 at a session of the Baltic assembly. Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele will report on the development of the Baltic customs union project.
- President Guntis Ulmanis backed closer economic ties and bilateral trade relations with Taiwan.
- Only 134 non-citizens received alien's passports from April 10 to April 18.
- The state revenue service revealed several faults with the accountancy at the institute of international relations, led by professor Juris Bojars.
- Interior Minister Dainis Turlais was appointed chairman of the working group to deal with modernising the eastern border.
- Ulmanis said recognition of the new alien's passports by Russia is a matter of time.
- An opinion poll carried out by the Central European magazine names Parex bank as best local bank in Latvia.
- The first quarter net profit of Unibanka was 1.37 million lats.
- Local governments in the eastern districts of Daugavpils and Kraslava drew up and approved a draft law which foresees the creation of an economic zone in Latgale, south eastern Latvia.
